title: EwsRegister: Exchange Web Services dependency discovery before the 2027 shutdown

problem_severity_frequency.rationale: A dated, non-negotiable EWS disablement (2026-10-01) and shutdown (2027-04-01) with hidden dependencies in backup jobs, archive connectors, public folders and scripts is adequately evidenced for this market by a credible secondary source; the breakage is one-time rather than frequent, which keeps this at 3.

buyer_budget_clarity.rationale: Buyer assumed (MSPs / SMB IT managers on Microsoft 365); no evidence of budget ownership or purchase. Capped at 2.

evidence_strength.rationale: Single credible secondary source about the platform change; no primary or buyer-side evidence.

differentiation.rationale: No defensible wedge: Microsoft's free authoritative EWS usage report plus `EWSEnabled` / `EWSAllowedAppIDs` controls cover the core need, and the residual work is one-shot migration services MSPs already sell. A first-party alternative makes this undifferentiable, capped at 2.

economics.rationale: A one-shot need priced as a subscription is a poor recurring business; support and spec-maintenance costs unmodelled. Modelled economics on untested inputs capped at 2.

economic_buyer.note: Buyer assumed (MSPs / SMB IT managers on Microsoft 365); no evidence anyone buys a standalone discovery tool rather than an MSP project.
economic_buyer.resolve_via: Ask 5 MSPs what they charge and what tools they use today.

painful_frequent_or_budgeted.note: Breakage is real and dated but infrequent (one-time), and the pain is the tenant's, not necessarily a budget holder's.
painful_frequent_or_budgeted.resolve_via: Buyer interviews on budget ownership for EWS migration.

non_paid_distribution.note: MSP communities and marketplaces are plausible; no prospects or channel identified.
non_paid_distribution.resolve_via: One MSP-community launch measured for qualified inbound.

defensible_wedge.note: Microsoft's free EWS usage report and `EWSEnabled` / `EWSAllowedAppIDs` controls already cover the core discovery need, and the residual work is one-shot migration services MSPs already sell.

no_network_effects_needed.note: A per-tenant scanner may be useful alone, but benchmark or cross-tenant value is unproven.
no_network_effects_needed.resolve_via: Confirm single-tenant utility satisfies the buyer.

plausible_margins.note: A one-shot need priced monthly is a poor recurring subscription; support and spec-maintenance costs unmodelled.
plausible_margins.resolve_via: Model 20 tenants and the post-migration job.

acceptable_risk.note: Reading a tenant's EWS usage needs Microsoft Graph permissions and a security review.

cheap_disconfirming_test.note: A zero-cost desk competitive scan was sufficient to disconfirm the wedge this run.

not_all_optimistic.note: Viability rests on several untested assumptions (buyer, willingness to pay, recurrence).
not_all_optimistic.resolve_via: Name and test the weakest assumption first.
